A.explanation: This divides the useful power $Fv$ by 4.0, which multiplies by efficiency instead of dividing by it.

B.explanation: This has units of $1/\text{power}$ and is the reciprocal of a power, so it cannot be an input power.

C.explanation: Useful output power is $Fv$ and input is output divided by 0.25, giving $4.0Fv$.

D.explanation: This divides force by velocity, giving units of $\text{N s m}^{-1}$, not the units of power $\text{W}$.

hints: Notice the car moves at constant velocity $v$ against resistive force $F$, so the engine driving force must equal $F$.
Recall useful output power for motion with force parallel to velocity is $P = Fv$.
Use efficiency $= 0.25 =$ output power divided by input power, and rearrange to find input power from $Fv$.
walkthrough: At constant velocity the resultant force is zero, so the forward driving force from the engine equals the resistive force $F$.
Useful output power is $P_{out} = Fv$ because power equals force times velocity when they are in the same direction.
Efficiency is defined as $\text{efficiency} = P_{out} / P_{in} = 25\% = 0.25$.
Substitute $P_{out} = Fv$ to get $P_{in} = Fv / 0.25 = 4.0Fv$. This is option C.
